in_english.name: Evangelist
in_english.meaning: one who proclaims the Gospel, announcer of good news
in_english.long_meaning: Evangelist - a term used in Christian tradition to describe a person who proclaims the Gospel of Jesus Christ, often associated with missionary work and the spread of the faith. The term is derived from the Greek Evangelion (εὐαγγέλιον), meaning good news or Gospel. In the New Testament, the term is used to describe the four authors of the Gospels, Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John. Modern usage may refer to individuals or groups who proclaim the Gospel, often with a focus on evangelism and mission.

biblical_reference.note: The term 'Evangelist' is used in the New Testament to describe the four authors of the Gospels, who proclaimed the good news of Jesus Christ.

saint_reference.saint_name: Saint Matthew, Saint Mark, Saint Luke, Saint John
saint_reference.note: The four Evangelists are also revered as saints in the Christian tradition, with their feast days observed on January 24 (Matthew), April 25 (Mark), October 18 (Luke), and December 27 (John).

data.cultural_impact: The title “Evangelist” holds great cultural significance as it represents the early Christian missionaries who played a pivotal role in spreading the teachings of Jesus Christ beyond the Middle East. The term has been used throughout history to refer to individuals who dedicated their lives to sharing the Gospel, often leading to the growth and expansion of Christian communities around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name “Evangelist” carries immense significance, not only for those who bear the title, but for all Christians. Evangelism is a vital call to action for every believer, rooted in the Great Commission given by Jesus to His disciples: “So go and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit” (Matthew 28:19). The name “Evangelist” serves as an inspiration and reminder that sharing the Good News is a fundamental aspect of our faith and a way to bring others closer to God.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Evangelist is derived from the Greek word euaggelios, meaning bearer of good news. The name Evangelist carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In Christian tradition, Evangelist refers to one of the four authors of the New Testament Gospels.

It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.
